Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: Wave 1 registers a broad set of falsifiable associations between measured genomic/biomarker predictors and CRISPR dependency scores, prioritizing biologically plausible biomarker-outcome pairings across all requested dependency outcomes. Direction convention is that more negative dependency means stronger dependency. Driver-alteration hypotheses expect enhanced dependency on the corresponding driver or downstream effector: KRAS mutation and stronger KRAS dependency; BRAF V600E and stronger BRAF dependency; EGFR amplification and stronger EGFR dependency; ERBB2 amplification and stronger ERBB2 dependency. Tumor suppressor/pathway hypotheses expect pathway-specific dependencies: KEAP1 loss and stronger NFE2L2 dependency; TP53 loss and weaker MDM2 dependency because MDM2 is most important when p53 is intact; SMARCA4/ARID1A loss and stronger SMARCA2 dependency as synthetic-lethal remodeling dependencies; MSI-high or BRCA2 loss and stronger WRN dependency under DNA-repair stress hypotheses. MYC amplification is tested against core transcription/translation/stress-response dependencies (POLR2A, RPL11, DHX9, USP7) to capture broad oncogenic transcriptional addiction and alternative MYC-stabilization pathways. KRAS mutation is tested against RIT1 with a weaker-dependency hypothesis because mutant KRAS may reduce reliance on upstream RIT1 signaling, while alternative models are possible. RB1 loss is tested against KIF18A because E2F-driven cell-cycle entry could increase dependence on mitotic kinesin function. PIK3CA mutation is tested against STAT3 because PI3K/AKT signaling can cooperate with STAT3. ERBB2 amplification is tested against TMED10 as a weaker secretory-trafficking dependence hypothesis. These are discovery associations only; none imply causality or generalizability until evidence and validation are assessed.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. record.narrative: Wave-1 discovery supports three very large, precise associations, but only two are in the registered hypothesized direction. H7 is accepted: SMARCA4 loss is associated with substantially stronger SMARCA2 dependency, signed estimate +0.784 with 95% interval entirely positive under direction -1. H9 is accepted: MSI-high is associated with substantially stronger WRN dependency, signed estimate +0.790 with interval entirely positive under direction -1. Because these are CRISPR dependency scores, more negative raw scores mean stronger dependency; these signed positive values under direction -1 correspond to raw negative differences, i.e., stronger dependency in the exposed groups. The magnitudes are far above the 10% clinical-significance scale relative to outcome means. H5 is rejected as originally registered. Its signed estimate is -0.796 with a 95% interval entirely negative under direction -1, so the data strongly favor the opposite raw contrast: KEAP1-loss cells have dependency_NFE2L2 that is about 0.796 units higher/less negative than KEAP1-wild-type cells. This is a very large association, but its sign contradicts the registered hypothesis that KEAP1 loss would produce stronger NFE2L2 dependency. The correct response is to register a reversed association proposal and independently validate the original comparison to check whether this anomalous direction is reproducible or reflects scale/coding/constructed-data behavior. H3 is borderline and remains unresolved: EGFR amplification has a point estimate of about 0.025 units of stronger EGFR dependency, roughly 10% of the outcome mean, but the signed interval includes zero, so multiplicity-adjusted or independent confirmation is needed before acceptance. The remaining driver and pathway hypotheses (H1, H2, H4, H6, H11, H12, H15, H17) show small signed effects with intervals crossing zero and generally near-null magnitudes; they are not accepted. Some remain active because driver hypotheses deserve focused follow-up, while lower-prior or untested claims are deferred. The follow-up proposals test whether the accepted effects are subtype-specific or confounded by correlated genomic markers (ARID1A loss for SMARCA4, KRAS mutation for EGFR) and whether the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 association remains after removing TP53-loss cells.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
The independent validation result R13 resolves the KEAP1/NFE2L2 sign anomaly. For the originally registered claim H5, with direction -1 (expected stronger NFE2L2 dependency under KEAP1 loss), validation gives signed estimate -0.7914, interval [-0.8213, -0.7615], entirely negative under the original direction. This confirms that the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is positive: KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less negative dependency_NFE2L2 than KEAP1-intact cells. Therefore the original hypothesis is rejected in this dataset, not merely unresolved. Because validation also supports the reversed association H19, with signed estimate +0.7914 and strict independent interval entirely positive under direction +1, I accept H19 as a dataset-level association: KEAP1 loss is associated with substantially weaker NFE2L2 dependency by about 0.79 dependency units, with discovery and validation estimates +0.796 and +0.791 respectively and intervals excluding zero. The magnitude is more than two outcome SDs and far above the 10% meaningful-scale threshold, although relative-difference interpretation is awkward because the overall outcome mean is close to zero. This remains an association, not evidence of causality or general biological behavior. I close H5 and the primary reversed claim H19 because the comparison is now well characterized in this dataset, while new proposals test context specificity and possible confounding.

The accepted wave-1 discoveries H7 and H9 remain important. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, and MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. However, neither has independent validation yet, and it is unclear whether these effects are stable across lineage subtype, culture type, correlated chromatin-remodeling losses, or other dataset structure. I therefore propose focused interaction and conditional analyses: lineage/culture heterogeneity for H7 and H9; ARID1A-loss heterogeneity for the SMARCA2 claim; and TP53-loss/lineage heterogeneity for the reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 association. I also propose research_marker_e_positive controls for SMARCA2, WRN, and NFE2L2. Because research_marker_e is a constructed binary assay with no assigned biological role, null associations for this marker would support specificity of the accepted effects; strong associations would indicate that the dataset may encode broader structure or technical confounding.

The remaining driver claims are still not accepted. H1 KRAS mutation remains near but not statistically convincing for stronger KRAS dependency; H3 EGFR amplification is borderline with signed estimate about +0.025 under direction -1 and interval crossing zero. I propose subtype follow-ups for KRAS and EGFR, while EGFR-specific KRAS-wild-type and adenocarcinoma subgroup claims already registered can be analyzed next. The next analysis should prioritize the registered H19 refinements, accepted-effect interaction tests, specificity controls, and EGFR/KRAS follow-ups. record.narrative: The next exploration wave focuses on three goals: (1) stress-test the accepted dataset associations, (2) probe whether near-null driver hypotheses are masked by lineage or constructed-marker structure, and (3) broaden coverage of outcomes that have not yet been analyzed. For the accepted effects, I register research_marker_d_positive as a constructed binary negative control. If marker D shows a large association with SMARCA2 or WRN, or an accepted effect changes materially across marker D-positive and marker D-negative cells, this would suggest that the large effects may partly reflect dataset encoding, confounding, or marker-correlated population structure rather than isolated genomic-loss associations. If marker D is near null and the accepted interaction differences are small, that increases confidence that the associations are specific to the genomic markers of interest. I likewise register media_serum_pct interactions to test whether serum condition modifies the SMARCA4/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, and KEAP1/NFE2L2 associations; this addresses whether these associations are robust across culture conditions. For near-null driver hypotheses, I add subtype-specific comparisons for BRAF V600E and ERBB2 amplification in adenocarcinoma, and marker-interaction tests for EGFR amplification and KRAS mutation. These are not claims of causality; they are diagnostics for heterogeneity and possible dataset confounding. I also reactivate deferred but biologically motivated comparisons, including ARID1A loss versus SMARCA2, BRCA2 loss versus WRN, MYC amplification versus DHX9/USP7, RB1 loss versus KIF18A, and ERBB2 amplification versus TMED10, so that the next analysis wave can still cover less-tested outcome-predictor pairs if the controller selects them.

prompt:
Iteration 2/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: This wave materially strengthens the specificity and robustness of the three currently accepted dataset associations. The constructed negative control research_marker_d_positive is near null for all three outcomes: SMARCA2 (R14), WRN (R15), and NFE2L2 (R16). Although these are not equivalence proofs, the point estimates are small relative to the main effects and the 95% intervals cross zero, so there is no evidence for a marker-D-specific association. Likewise, the marker-D interaction tests on the accepted effects are near null: SMARCA4/SMARCA2 (R17), MSI-high/WRN (R18), and KEAP1/NFE2L2 (R19). The adenocarcinoma interaction for MSI-high/WRN is also small and imprecise around zero (R23), consistent with a broadly shared effect rather than a subtype-restricted one. These results reduce concern that the large associations are driven by random dataset structure correlated with marker D. Conditional analyses also remain very large: SMARCA4-loss cells in adenocarcinoma (R20) and SMARCA4-loss cells restricted to ARID1A-intact cells (R21) both show signed effects about 0.78 under direction -1, meaning raw SMARCA2 dependency is roughly 0.78 units more negative than in the comparator group. MSI-high cells in adenocarcinoma similarly show about 0.78 signed effect under direction -1 (R22). The reversed KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is present and large in both TP53-intact (R24) and TP53-loss (R25) cells, with signed estimates about 0.79 and 0.81 under direction +1, meaning raw NFE2L2 dependency is higher/less negative in KEAP1-loss cells by about the same magnitude in both genomic contexts. I therefore accept these conditional/subgroup associations as dataset-specific evidence: SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency in the adenocarcinoma subtype and independently of ARID1A loss; MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency in the adenocarcinoma subtype; KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency in both TP53-intact and TP53-loss cells. I reject the marker-D and heterogeneity interaction claims because their estimates are negligible and intervals include zero. Given that the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 claim has the largest cell counts among accepted primary associations and has survived the main confounding checks, I request independent validation for H7 before validating WRN/MSI-high. These conclusions remain dataset associations, not causal or generalizable findings.

record.narrative: The independent validation result for H7 is strongly supportive. Under the registered direction -1, validation R26 gives a signed estimate of +0.8006 with an independent interval entirely positive, [0.7713, 0.8300], at alpha=0.003846. Because the estimate is already signed to the hypothesis direction, the raw SMARCA4-loss minus SMARCA4-intact difference in dependency_SMARCA2 is approximately -0.80, meaning SMARCA4-loss cells have substantially more negative dependency_SMARCA2 scores, i.e., stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Discovery R7 was consistent: signed estimate +0.7840, interval [0.7646, 0.8034]. The validation estimate is nearly identical to discovery and the independent interval excludes zero even under a stringent multiplicity-adjusted threshold. The magnitude is very large: it is more than two outcome SDs and far exceeds the 10% meaningful-difference threshold, although relative-difference framing is awkward because dependency scores are centered near zero. I therefore accept H7 as a robust, independently validated dataset-level association: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. I close H7 as the primary claim because the direction and magnitude are now well characterized in this dataset. This association is biologically plausible as a synthetic-lethality-like relationship, but the data remain associational; they do not establish causality or generalizability beyond this dataset. The most informative next analysis is independent validation of H9, MSI-high versus WRN dependency, which is the next accepted but not yet independently validated large effect. Negative findings from prior robustness tests remain meaningful: the original H5 KEAP1/NFE2L2 hypothesis is rejected and reversed H19 is validated; marker-D negative controls and marker-D interactions for SMARCA2, WRN, and NFE2L2 are null/close-to-null; and the WRN subtype interaction is null. Conditional accepted subgroup effects for SMARCA2 and WRN remain consistent but are not independently validated and should be interpreted only as dataset-specific subgroup associations. Many driver-gene hypotheses remain unresolved or unresolved near-null and should not be presented as supported.

record.narrative: I select twelve discovery analyses that most directly stress-test the currently accepted dataset associations before requesting independent validation for MSI-high/WRN. For each major association (SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2), I run marker F negative-control main effects and marker F interactions. Marker D controls and marker D interactions were near null; a consistent marker F null pattern would reduce concern that the large effects are artifacts of arbitrary constructed-marker encoding or marker-correlated structure. I also run screen_batch_a interactions for all three accepted exposures to assess whether the effects are stable across screen batch rather than driven by batch-correlated structure. I include the adherent-culture MSI-high/WRN main effect as a direct context-specific robustness check before validation. Finally, I include two specificity checks: ARID1A loss among SMARCA4-intact cells to test whether SMARCA2 dependency is specific to SMARCA4 loss rather than generalized SWI/SNF-loss biology, and BRCA2 loss among MSI-negative cells to test whether WRN dependency has DNA-repair associations beyond MSI-high status. I defer the lower-priority mutual-exclusivity-restricted KRAS/BRAF driver tests because they concern currently near-null driver claims and are less important than validating the robustness of the three large accepted associations.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: This wave adds marker-F negative controls, batch interaction tests, an adherent-culture MSI-high/WRN analysis, and two specificity analyses. The marker-F controls are close to null for all three major outcomes: WRN (R27), SMARCA2 (R31), and NFE2L2 (R35). The marker-F interactions with the accepted associations are also near null for SMARCA2 (R32), WRN (R28), and NFE2L2 (R36). Together with the earlier marker-D null controls and null interactions, these results reduce concern that the very large SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 associations are artifacts of arbitrary constructed-marker structure or marker-correlated population structure. Batch tests for MSI-high/WRN and KEAP1/NFE2L2 are near null (R29, R37), although the WRN batch interaction is imprecise because the exposed cells in batch_a are small. The SMARCA2 batch_a interaction is statistically nonzero but small in magnitude and opposite to the registered negative-direction claim; it does not support the claim as registered and is far smaller than the main SMARCA4 effect, so I reject it for that claim rather than treating it as a meaningful confounder. The adherent-culture MSI-high/WRN effect is very large and precise (R30: signed estimate +0.813, 95% CI [0.780,0.846] under direction -1), consistent with the overall MSI-high/WRN effect (R8) and the adenocarcinoma-restricted effect (R22). The ARID1A-loss effect among SMARCA4-intact cells is null (R34), supporting specificity of the SMARCA2 signal to SMARCA4 loss rather than generalized SWI/SNF loss. The BRCA2-loss effect among MSI-negative cells is null (R38), suggesting the WRN association is not a broad DNA-repair-loss marker but is more specific to MSI-high status in this dataset. Given this robustness pattern, I request independent validation for H9, MSI-high versus WRN dependency, because it is the next accepted large association and has now survived marker controls, subtype, culture, and specificity checks.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: The newly delivered validation strengthens the main set of supported dataset-specific associations. For H5, the original hypothesis that KEAP1 loss is associated with stronger NFE2L2 dependency remains rejected. The independent validation R13, registered under direction -1, is signed negative, estimate -0.791 with an independent interval entirely negative, [-0.821, -0.761]. Because estimates are already signed to the registered direction, this negative result indicates that the raw KEAP1-loss minus KEAP1-intact difference in dependency_NFE2L2 is positive: KEAP1-loss cells have higher, less negative dependency_NFE2L2 scores. Thus validation confirms the direction reversal captured by H19 rather than the original H5 direction. For H9, independent validation R39 strongly supports the MSI-high association: signed estimate +0.8215 with an independent interval entirely positive, [0.766, 0.877], at the validation alpha threshold. This is consistent with discovery R8, signed estimate +0.7899. The raw interpretation is that MSI-high cells have dependency_WRN scores about 0.82 units lower, i.e. much stronger WRN dependency. The magnitude is more than three WRN outcome SDs and far exceeds a 10% relative-difference threshold when interpreted cautiously, although relative ratios are awkward because dependency scores are centered near zero. H9 is therefore accepted as an independently validated dataset-level association and closed as a primary claim. For H20, independent validation R40 supports the TP53-intact KEAP1 context: signed estimate +0.7948 with independent interval [0.764, 0.826], consistent with discovery R24. This confirms that the KEAP1-loss association with weaker NFE2L2 dependency is large in TP53-intact cells, while prior discovery H26 indicates a similar large effect in TP53-loss cells, though H26 itself has not been independently validated. Overall supported associations now include: SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, validated by R7/R26; MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency, validated by R8/R39; and KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, validated in the reversed H19 and in the TP53-intact conditional H20. The accepted set also includes large conditional/context claims: SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency in adenocarcinoma and ARID1A-intact cells; MSI-high WRN dependency in adenocarcinoma and adherent culture; and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 dependency in TP53-loss cells. Negative and robustness findings remain meaningful: original H5 is rejected; marker D and marker F constructed controls are near null for SMARCA2, WRN, and NFE2L2; marker D/F interactions are near null; the WRN subtype interaction is null; ARID1A loss in SMARCA4-intact cells is null for SMARCA2; and BRCA2 loss in MSI-negative cells is null for WRN. The most informative next work is to complete the marker-E control suite, test media-serum and other culture/technical contexts, and continue to probe remaining driver and MYC-associated hypotheses without claiming causality or generalizability. All conclusions remain associations within this supplied dataset, not causal or external-validity claims.

record.narrative: This wave adds focused robustness and context checks for the three large accepted associations: SMARCA4 loss -> stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high -> stronger WRN dependency, and KEAP1 loss -> weaker NFE2L2 dependency. First, I register main effects within the dominant Avana library and, where cell numbers are expected to be adequate, within the KY library. These library-specific effects test whether the associations are library-dependent or persist across CRISPR screen platforms. For SMARCA2 and NFE2L2, I also register Avana-versus-non-Avana interactions to test technical stability. For WRN, I avoid a library interaction because MSI-high is a relatively small exposed group and the non-Avana exposed cell could fall below the required cell count. Second, I register interactions with proliferation rate, mutation burden, ploidy, and 10% serum media context to test whether the accepted effects are stable after stratification on cell-state and genomic-instability proxies. A near-null interaction would support robustness; a large interaction would indicate that the effect is concentrated in particular proliferative, mutational, ploidy, or serum contexts. Third, I add a STK11 co-loss interaction for the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association because KEAP1 and STK11 co-loss biology is common in lung adenocarcinoma-like lines; a null interaction would make the KEAP1 association less likely to be a co-loss artifact. These proposals complement already registered marker-E controls, marker-E interactions, culture-type adherence checks, media 5% main effects, and media 10% interactions. All remain dataset-specific associations and are not causal or generalizability claims.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, so I use the analysis slot to stress-test the currently accepted large dataset associations and complete the constructed-marker control suite. First, I request marker-E main effects for the three major outcomes: SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-loss cells (H34), WRN dependency among MSI-high cells (H35), and NFE2L2 dependency among KEAP1-loss cells (H36). Marker D and marker F main effects were near null; marker E is the remaining arbitrary binary control before deciding whether any constructed marker encodes meaningful structure or merely serves as a negative control. Second, I request library-context main effects for the accepted associations: Avana-restricted SMARCA2/SMARCA4, WRN/MSI-high, and NFE2L2/KEAP1 effects (H73, H74, H75), plus KY-restricted SMARCA2/SMARCA4 and NFE2L2/KEAP1 effects (H76, H77). I omit a KY-restricted WRN analysis because MSI-high is a small exposed subgroup and the KY-exposed cell could be too imprecise; Avana is the dominant library, while KY provides a second platform check for the two larger binary exposures. Third, I request targeted moderation tests: growth-rate median-split interactions for SMARCA2/SMARCA4 and WRN/MSI-high (H80, H81), mutation-burden median-split interaction for WRN/MSI-high (H84), and STK11 co-loss interaction for NFE2L2/KEAP1 (H92). These test whether the accepted effects are stable across proliferation context, whether the WRN association is merely a proxy for hypermutation, and whether the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is robust to KEAP1-STK11 co-loss structure. I defer media-serum main effects, ploidy interactions, library-interaction tests, marker-E interactions, and remaining driver/MYC hypotheses until after these more direct robustness checks. Near-null marker-E or moderation tests, and consistent library-subset effects, would strengthen the conclusion that the accepted associations are meaningful dataset-level signals rather than artifacts of marker encoding, library platform, proliferation, mutation burden, or co-loss context. All selected contrasts remain associations within this dataset; no causal or external-validity claim is implied.

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: This wave provides strong robustness evidence for the three accepted large associations and completes the constructed-marker negative-control suite. Marker-E main effects are all close to zero for SMARCA2, WRN, and NFE2L2 (H34/H35/H36). Combined with the earlier marker-D and marker-F null controls, these results make it less plausible that the very large accepted signals are artifacts of the arbitrary constructed-marker encoding or marker-correlated structure; I therefore reject the marker-E association claims and close them. Library-restricted main effects are highly concordant with the overall effects. SMARCA4 loss predicts much stronger SMARCA2 dependency in both the dominant Avana library and the KY library, and MSI-high predicts much stronger WRN dependency in Avana. KEAP1 loss again predicts weaker NFE2L2 dependency in both Avana and KY. These library-specific effects are large and precise, so I accept H73-H77 as context-specific dataset associations and close them. Moderation tests are less supportive of an important effect-size interaction. The growth-rate interaction for SMARCA4/SMARCA2 (H80) is statistically marginal but opposite to the registered negative direction; raw interaction is small and positive, not practically meaningful compared with the main effect near -0.8, so I reject H80 rather than promoting an opposite small interaction. The growth-rate interaction for MSI-high/WRN (H81) is imprecise and does not support the registered negative direction. The mutation-burden interaction for MSI-high/WRN (H84) is invalid because the low-burden complement contains no MSI-high cells; this indicates structural overlap between MSI status and mutation burden in this dataset rather than a meaningful null interaction. The STK11 co-loss interaction for KEAP1/NFE2L2 (H92) is near null and does not support direction-specific moderation. I request independent validation for H26, the TP53-loss-specific KEAP1/NFE2L2 association, because it is an accepted large context effect not yet independently validated and validating it would complete the KEAP1/NFE2L2 assessment across both TP53 strata.

record.narrative: The new validation evidence confirms both due claims and strengthens the core set of supported dataset-specific associations. For H7, SMARCA4 loss versus SMARCA4 intact in dependency_SMARCA2, the independent validation R26 is signed positive for the registered negative-direction claim: estimate +0.8006 with an independent interval [0.7713, 0.8300]. Because estimates are already signed to the hypothesis direction, the raw interpretation is that SMARCA4-loss lines have much more negative dependency_SMARCA2 scores than SMARCA4-intact lines, i.e. much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Discovery R7 and validation R26 are highly concordant in magnitude and direction, so H7 remains accepted and closed. For H26, KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact in dependency_NFE2L2 within TP53-loss cells, validation R53 is signed positive for the registered positive-direction claim: estimate +0.8046 with an independent interval [0.7383, 0.8708]. The raw interpretation is that TP53-loss KEAP1-loss cells have less negative dependency_NFE2L2 scores than TP53-loss KEAP1-intact cells, i.e. weaker NFE2L2 dependency. This is consistent with discovery R25 and with the independently validated TP53-intact conditional claim H20, where R40 estimated a very similar effect. Thus the KEAP1/NFE2L2 association is large in both TP53 strata and is independently validated for the TP53-loss stratum. Overall, the strongest evidence now supports three large associations in this supplied dataset: SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high status with much stronger WRN dependency, and KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The latter has been validated both overall as a reversed claim H19 and in TP53-intact H20 and TP53-loss H26 strata. Negative or null robustness evidence also constrains interpretation: constructed marker D/E/F main effects and interactions are near null; ARID1A loss is not associated with SMARCA2 dependency among SMARCA4-intact cells; BRCA2 loss is not associated with WRN dependency among MSI-negative cells; and batch, lineage-subtype, culture, and library subset checks have not materially overturned the main effects. Remaining uncertainty concerns whether the large associations depend on culture media, Cas9 activity, ploidy, other co-mutations, or molecular context, and whether other measured predictors or subgroups show scientifically meaningful differences. The next most informative analyses are formal interaction tests for the accepted effects across additional technical and culture contexts, completion of the registered media-serum and Cas9 stress tests, TP53 interaction testing for KEAP1/NFE2L2, and broader driver/MYC hypothesis tests such as KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, ERBB2, MYC, RB1, PIK3CA, and DNA-repair predictors. All conclusions should be interpreted as associations within this supplied dataset, not causal effects or externally generalizable findings.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

NF1 loss activates RAS signaling, and in the absence of KRAS mutation this may reveal dependency on endogenous KRAS signaling. I also test ERBB2 amplification among KRAS-wild-type cells because KRAS mutation can bypass EGFR/ERBB2 dependence; an association in KRAS-wild-type cells would be more informative for RTK dependency than an unselected analysis.

Third, I refine MYC hypotheses. Amplification alone may be too blunt, so I restrict MYC-amplification effects to cells above a high MYC-expression threshold. DHX9, USP7, POLR2A, and RPL11 are plausible MYC-associated vulnerabilities involving replication stress, protein stability, transcription, and translation. If MYC amplification is a biologically meaningful driver state only when accompanied by high MYC expression, these expression-restricted effects may be larger than the near-null amplification-only effects. record.narrative:
No assessments are due, so I register new scientifically motivated comparisons while preserving existing unresolved robustness checks. The prior run established three very large dataset associations, but most other measured predictors remain either small or untested. I therefore add targeted biology and robustness questions.

First, I test MDM2 dependency through the p14ARF/MTAP/CDKN2A axis restricted to TP53-intact cells. CDKN2A encodes p14ARF, which inhibits MDM2; loss of CDKN2A could increase MDM2 pathway activity and therefore stronger MDM2 dependency, represented by a more negative dependency_MDM2 score. I register CDKN2A-loss versus CDKN2A-intact and MTAP-loss versus MTAP-intact in TP53-intact cells, both expected negative. MTAP is frequently co-deleted near CDKN2A and can proxy similar p14ARF/CDKN2A locus biology, so concordance would support a coherent axis; a large CDKN2A-only effect would favor CDKN2A-specific structure.

Second, I test more biologically selected RAS-pathway and RTK hypotheses. Direct KRAS-mutant versus wild-type effects were tiny, so I ask whether NF1 loss in KRAS-wild-type cells predicts stronger KRAS dependency. NF1 loss activates RAS signaling, and in the absence of KRAS mutation this may reveal dependency on endogenous KRAS signaling. I also test ERBB2 amplification among KRAS-wild-type cells because KRAS mutation can bypass EGFR/ERBB2 dependence; an association in KRAS-wild-type cells would be more informative for RTK dependency than an unselected analysis.

Third, I refine MYC hypotheses. Amplification alone may be too blunt, so I restrict MYC-amplification effects to cells above a high MYC-expression threshold. DHX9, USP7, POLR2A, and RPL11 are plausible MYC-associated vulnerabilities involving replication stress, protein stability, transcription, and translation. If MYC amplification is a biologically meaningful driver state only when accompanied by high MYC expression, these expression-restricted effects may be larger than the near-null amplification-only effects. If they remain small, MYC amplification is unlikely to be a strong predictor of these dependencies in this dataset.

Fourth, I add specificity and robustness checks for the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 signal. The prior STK11 co-loss interaction was near null, but a main effect restricted to STK11-intact cells can test whether the large positive effect is an artifact of KEAP1-STK11 co-deletion. I register KEAP1 loss versus KEAP1 intact among STK11-intact cells, with the registered positive direction matching the accepted weaker-NFE2L2-dependency association.

Finally, I test screen-quality moderation using screen_roc_auc median split. For accepted SMARCA2 and WRN effects, a near-null interaction would support stability; a more negative interaction would suggest stronger associations in higher-quality screens. For the KEAP1/NFE2L2 positive association, I use positive interaction direction for the same logic. These are dataset-level robustness checks, not external-validity claims.

I prioritize comparisons with adequate expected cell counts and avoid structurally impossible strata. Large, precise main effects would motivate later validation; near-zero MYC or screen-quality interactions would mainly narrow the space of additional predictors and support robustness of the accepted associations. All claims remain associations within this supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable findings.
